title: The tide won't notice
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
arc: The Last Week of the Century
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Gully asks the uncle about the millennium. The uncle says the tide won't notice. Gully asks what will. The uncle says the computers, and he hasn't got one. Wood draws the tide table on the wall: it goes to 2000 already.

panels.composition: The shack. The UNCLE at the stove. GULLY. WOOD with BARNABY on a crab pot.

image.prompt: inside a bait shack: an old man at a small stove, a teenager, a young man with a dog on a crab pot, black and white, no words

balloons.text: Computers is what they say. I haven't got one.
Then the paper's got a problem.

image.prompt: an old weathered man at a stove, flat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The tide table tacked to the wall: a column of dates going past the 31st into a year that starts with a 2. Already printed. Already there.

image.prompt: close on a tide table tacked to a shack wall with its column of dates running past the year's end, black and white, no words
image.notes: The dates as shapes; the 2 legible. Letter after: nothing more.

panels.composition: The three of them and the dog in the shack, the stove, the table on the wall. Friday's tide, printed in October. The strip finds this reassuring and doesn't say so.

image.prompt: three figures and a dog inside a warm bait shack with a tide table on the wall and rain on the window, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: 'Tide comes in.' The table already goes to 2000.
